data.body:
IMPLEMENTED (rebar-debug Phase 2). Summary of the change and the evidence behind each number.

## Where the per-model floors came from

Anthropic's PUBLISHED table, not the brackets:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
(section "Minimum cacheable prompt length", read 2026-08-02). The ticket's two independent
measurements were used only to VERIFY it, and all three agree:

    sonnet-4-6    922 no / 1042 cached (w1035 r1035)   => ~1024        doc 1024  OK
    sonnet-4-5    253 no / 7930 cached                 => <=1024       doc 1024  OK
    haiku-4-5    2748 no / 4749 cached (w4742 r4742)   => (2748,4749]  doc 4096  OK

The published table is NOT monotonic across generations (512 on opus-5/fable-5/mythos-5, 1024 on
opus-4-8/sonnet-5/sonnet-4-6/sonnet-4-5, 2048 on opus-4-7, 4096 on opus-4-6/opus-4-5/haiku-4-5),
which is exactly why one global could not express it.

Sharpest consequence, not previously called out on the ticket: `claude-opus-4-8` is rebar's
DEFAULT_MODEL and its documented floor is 1024, so the 4096 global was 4x too high on the model
rebar runs most — not just on sonnet.

## Bedrock deliberately left on the conservative fallback

Anthropic's table states these minimums apply on every platform EXCEPT Amazon Bedrock, which
publishes its own. rebar has measured none of Bedrock's, so `_cache_min_prefix_tokens` is gated on
`prompt_cache_style == "anthropic"` and a Bedrock model falls through to CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS
rather than being assigned a guessed number. Same rule for any unlisted model id.

## The compared quantity

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` now takes `marked_prefix_tokens` and `cache_min_prefix_tokens`. With
the marked prefix known it emits one of two mutually exclusive reports:

  A. marked prefix >= floor, zero/zero  -> "was cacheable, cache silently did not engage"
                                           (the original story-S3 signal, retargeted)
  B. marked prefix <  floor AND a floor's worth of payload rides unmarked after the breakpoint
                                        -> names the marked-prefix size and the floor, i.e. the
                                           CHANGEABLE thing, instead of reporting the total

Case B is bounded by `unmarked >= floor` on purpose. Firing on every small marked prefix would
re-create precisely the ~20-lines-per-run spam bug 7a79 removed; the signal being made is "a
cacheable-sized payload is riding outside the breakpoint", not "the prefix is small".

`marked_prefix_tokens=None` keeps the pre-existing total-based predicate byte-for-byte, so every
un-updated caller and all of 7a79's semantics are untouched (pinned by a test).

## Threading

`runner.py` supplies both: `caps.cache_min_prefix_tokens`, and
`structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens(cache_settings, system_prompt=req.system_prompt)`.
That helper returns None unless an instructions breakpoint is actually set, and deliberately does
NOT size tool definitions (not available at that seam) — both conservatisms UNDER-count, which can
only suppress a warning, never manufacture one.

## Deliberately NOT done

`provenance_for` was left alone. Adding a 5th key to its `capabilities` record would change the
bytes of already-signed gate verdicts; the floor is a published property of the model, recoverable
from the recorded model id, so it does not need to ride in the signed record.

`plan_review/pass1.py`'s warm-up gate still reads the conservative global rather than the per-model
floor. Out of this ticket's file budget and out of its ACs. The direction is safe (it may skip
warming a prefix that would in fact have cached, i.e. a missed optimisation, never a wrong result),
but it is a real follow-up: on opus-4-8 the warm gate is now demanding 4x more prefix than the
provider does.

## Verification

tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py (17 tests), RED before the fix for the right reasons
(missing attribute / missing kwarg). Mutation-checked BOTH directions: re-introducing the
model-blind global returns 6 tests to RED; re-introducing the total-input_tokens comparison returns
the large-total/small-marked-prefix test to RED; restoring the fix returns all 17 to GREEN.
